minutes.headline: Assessors will recommend a single (not split) tax rate and rejecting all three optional exemptions for FY2026
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors reviewed FY2026 valuation and growth figures, worked through mapping and MUNIS data delays, and discussed hiring a third party to redo property neighborhoods after a citizen work group flagged inconsistent boundaries. Most of the meeting was spent line-editing a classification-hearing presentation, ending in board recommendations to reject the residential, open-space, and small commercial exemptions and to keep a single tax rate, plus review of a fall town meeting exemption/COLA warrant article and website fixes.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of September 4th as amended (motor vehicle abatement batch and updated DLS Clause 41C income/asset limits)
Approve two previously-held executive session minutes (dated 8/19 and 7/29)
Reject adoption of the residential exemption for the FY2026 classification
Reject adoption of the small commercial exemption for the FY2026 classification
Recommend a single (not split) tax rate for FY2026 rather than a split rate

budget_items.what_was_said: The principal assessor pointed the board to the LA-4 and comparison reports showing residential values increased for FY2026.

budget_items.topic: Total valuation change across all classes
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member asked for and was shown the overall total valuation change summed across all property classes, not just residential.
The assessor explained that agricultural and forest land values dropped because Chapter land per-acre crop values are set annually by the Farm Bureau and the state Department of Agriculture.
Staff reported the new growth figure that will appear in the LA-13 growth report.
Staff said they cleared a backlog of motor vehicle excise abatements, with more already piling up behind it.

budget_items.topic: DLS Clause 41C senior exemption income/asset limits
budget_items.what_was_said: Minutes corrections reflected new DLS-approved Clause 41C limits, raising the income limit and the asset limits for single and married applicants.
The board needed to sign an annual software maintenance bill from Vision for the assessing system.

budget_items.topic: Cost of adopting COLA-linked exemption clauses (warrant article)
budget_items.what_was_said: The assessor said the printed warrant article incorrectly showed zero cost; adopting the COLA adjustment clauses actually carries a small real cost to the town that needs correcting before town meeting.

budget_items.topic: Number of residents on Clause 41C exemption
budget_items.what_was_said: The board discussed and corrected the number of residents currently receiving the Clause 41C senior exemption for the warrant materials.

budget_items.topic: Incremental tax impact of COLA exemption adoption, funded from overlay
budget_items.what_was_said: The assessor said exemptions are paid out of the overlay account with only partial state reimbursement, and calculated the incremental cost shifted to other taxpayers from adopting the COLA update.
In discussing warrant costs a board member cited a prior year's minor cost from a similar exemption item.

budget_items.topic: Number of effective tax rates from exemptions plus a split rate
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member noted that combining the exemptions under discussion with a split tax rate could effectively create several different tax rates depending on property type.

budget_items.topic: Small business owner's estimate of split-rate tax impact
budget_items.what_was_said: The board relayed a local small commercial property owner's estimate that a split tax rate could raise their taxes sharply, potentially forcing relocation and cutting community donations.

budget_items.topic: FY2026 tax base composition by property class
budget_items.what_was_said: The presentation showed Lunenburg's tax base is overwhelmingly residential, with commercial, industrial and personal property combined well under the share DOR recommends before considering a split rate.
The presentation highlighted that the median single-family home value crossed a threshold for the first time, up from the prior year.

budget_items.topic: Placeholder FY2026 tax levy used for rate scenarios
budget_items.what_was_said: Lacking final Gateway data from the finance director, the assessor used a levy figure from an earlier budget task force exercise to model tax rate scenarios.

budget_items.topic: FY2026 estimated tax bill scenarios under CIP shift options
budget_items.what_was_said: The presentation modeled sample tax bills for several home values and a commercial property under different CIP shift scenarios, showing commercial bills rising much faster than residential bills fall.

budget_items.topic: Example CIP shift impact on a $600,000 commercial property
budget_items.what_was_said: Under a larger CIP shift, a sample $600,000 commercial property's tax bill was shown rising sharply compared with the single-rate baseline.

budget_items.topic: Historical valuation and tax rate trend
budget_items.what_was_said: The board reviewed a history slide showing valuation dipped briefly around 2022-2023 after certain lake-area properties were revalued, then rose sharply after a full revaluation the following year.

decisions.decision: Add a resident outreach conference on abatements/exemptions to the November 20 agenda for further planning.
Postpone review of the October 2 and October 16 minutes to the next meeting.
Board leaned toward hiring a third-party company, rather than the citizen work group, to review and reassign property neighborhoods.
Board took no formal position on the open-space discount exemption since Lunenburg has no land classified as open space for tax purposes.

Assessor said she fixed a software glitch causing an empty site-index page and agreed to look at adding a table of contents, removing a duplicate directory, and adding a revision-control log similar to the Board of Health's.
Reaffirmed that no further changes will be made to the assessors' website without board approval.
Scheduled the next meetings for November 20 at Town Hall, and tentatively December 3 and December 18, pending room availability.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors recommended a single, not split, tax rate for FY2026.
The board voted to reject adopting the residential exemption for the FY2026 classification.
The board also voted to reject adopting the small commercial exemption for FY2026.
The board leaned toward hiring an outside firm, rather than the citizen work group, to redo property-neighborhood boundaries after inconsistencies were flagged.
The assessor said the printed fall town meeting warrant article understated the cost of adopting COLA-linked exemption updates as zero and said it needs correcting before town meeting.

why_it_matters: A single versus split tax rate changes how the tax levy is divided between residential and commercial/industrial property, which shows up directly in individual tax bills.
Declining the residential and small commercial exemptions means the classification hearing will not shift additional tax burden between property types beyond the rate decision itself.

The COLA-linked exemption warrant article, once its cost is corrected, goes to voters at fall town meeting and is paid from the overlay account, meaning any expansion is funded by other taxpayers rather than the town budget.
